Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Rod Woodson is one of the greatest defensive backs in NFL history, but before he ever made it to the league, he and his family faced plenty of racially charged hatred growing up in Indiana. Woodson, who was raised by a Black father and a white mother, said that some people didn’t accept his family because they were biracial, including members of his own family. Recently, Woodson opened up about one particularly terrifying night from his childhood as the Pro Football Hall of Famer said that when he was 11 years old, the Ku Klux Klan tried to burn down his family’s home, and later sent them a letter threatening to do it again. Growing Up Biracial in Indiana Woodson was born in 1965 and grew up in Fort Wayne, Indiana. His father was from Gallatin, Tennessee, while his mother was from Fort Wayne. Appearing on OutKick’s The Craig Carton Show , Woodson said that both sides of his family had people who wanted nothing to do with them. “My dad’s side of the family, some of them didn’t like us cause we’re half white because they had that bias in them. And then you know, my mother family is from the north and then some half of them didn’t like us because we was half black,” Woodson said, on the show . Woodson said that he didn’t forget about that once he made it to the NFL. “I remember my dad’s side of the family wanted some tickets to a game and I told my dad, I said, ‘I love you. I’m going to give you tickets. I’ll give them tickets at this time, this one time for you, but they can never ever get tickets from me again.’ Because they didn’t want to be around us when I was a kid, so don’t be around me now,” he said. Woodson went on to star at Purdue before becoming one of the best defensive backs of his era. He played 17 seasons with the Pittsburgh Steelers, San Francisco 49ers, Baltimore Ravens, and Oakland Raiders, made 11 Pro Bowls, and won a Super Bowl with the Ravens after the 2000 season. item.title: Patriots vs. Packers weather forecast for NFL Week 9
item.description: The New England Patriots’ game in Miami last Sunday was partially played in miserable weather. This week’s contest against the Green Bay Packers will see a return to better playing conditions. The Patriots will be hosting the Packers at Gillette Stadium for a battle of 5-3 teams, with kickoff scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET. At that point in time, WBZ Boston projects temperatures of 56°F, which will drop to 52°F at the half and into the high 40s toward the end of the game — noticeably cooler than last week, but most importantly with minimal if any precipitation in the forecast. “The good news is the risk of rain looks to be decreasing, clouds breaking apart,” said meteorologist Sarah Wrobleski on Friday morning. “But temperatures will fall from the mid-50s into the upper 40s, and we’ll have a breezy wind, too.” That wind is projected to bring gusts of up to 24 mph, which could create challenging patterns inside the Patriots’ home arena. As a reminder, the two teams have had some kicking issues so far this season: New England’s Andy Borregales has made 30 of his 34 combined field goal and extra points (88.2%), with Green Bay’s Trey Smack at only 27-for-35 (77.2%) — giving him the lowest success rate in the league. Similar projections are also shared by other outlets such as NFL Weather or the National Weather Service . If those turn out to be accurate, Sunday would become the Patriots’ coldest contest of the season so far. It would also be the first to see temperatures drop into the 40s over the course of the game.

item.description: Oct 31, 2026; Louisville, Kentucky, USA; Louisville Cardinals quarterback Lincoln Kienholz (3) rushes the ball during the third quarter against Stanford Cardinal at L&N Federal Credit Union Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Chris Carter-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect It took until the second half, but Louisville started to get more aggressive with their linebackers. On this play, Stanquan Clark times up the snap before shooting the gap to make a play in the backfield. He’s just unlucky because the play goes to the other side, which leaves him grasping for air. Stanford uses motion again on this play with a full shift of their tight ends across the field. Louisville tracks the motion, but you will notice that no one picks up the running back coming out of the backfield. So, on this play, Stanford takes advantage of two different issues UofL had in coverage earlier in the game. They don’t identify their responsibility after the motion, and they don’t account for the running back out of the backfield on a short-yardage pass. This is a nice play design and call by Stanford, but it would be nice to be able to say that the play just beat Louisville as opposed to the defense not even giving itself a chance. Lincoln Kienholz had his weekly instalment of “Man, it’s nice to have a quarterback who can do this” in the second quarter with his arm, but he does it with his legs on this play. I especially love the spin move that wasn’t really needed. I wrote about Louisville needing to attack the edges of Stanford’s defense in the What To Watch For post last week, so I was really happy to see them try to get outside a lot in this game. The first drive of the game was edge runs and swing passes, and they came back to it in the third quarter for this nice touchdown. As good as Isaac Brown is in space, he should buy dinner for Jaleel Skinner and TJ McWilliams for their blocking on this play. McWilliams is the outside receiver to the top of the screen. He gets up to the outside linebacker, who is flowing towards him before passing him off to Skinner, who gets outside after going in motion. McWilliams then moves up to the cornerback to create a tunnel for Isaac to run through. This is teach tape. I’m a bit of a broken record on this, but I don’t really understand why they can run this defense as often as they run Cover 3. Situations will dictate a lot of things, but the only real difference is that they are a little more spread out. But if this were first down, you would not be blitzing Kaleb Perry, who loops around on a stunt on this play. He would be right in the middle of the field to play the run. Ben Perry would also not be in press coverage in the slot. He would be backed off a bit and could react to a run play. item.title: Danks offers Bayern squad update and discusses potential changes for Mainz clash
item.description: Danks offers Bayern squad update and discusses potential changes for Mainz clash Still in charge in Vincent Kompany's absence, Bayern Munich assistant coach Aaron Danks gave an update on his squad ahead of Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Mainz during a press conference on Friday. Danks revealed that Jamal Musiala and Aleksandar Pavlovic have both returned from injury to train with the team ahead of the game. “Most players trained yesterday. Jamal Musiala has re-joined the group, which is very positive. But tomorrow's game comes too soon for him. Aleks Pavlovic was also involved. We need to see how his legs react. Manuel Neuer trained again. Things look good there for the game,” Danks said. Asked about Musiala and Luis Diaz, who is also progressing in his recovery from injury, Danks said: "I think it's tough to set a date or game for their return. Next week they'll train individually and then be in full team training when everyone's back from the national teams. But there's no deadline." The Bayern assistant coach also revealed that some players could be rested, with Alphonso Davies among those who may need a break amid a congested schedule. “With a few players we need to look at workload and whether we rest them. Alphonso Davies, for example, needs a rest for his explosive nature. We'll make the decision today,” he said. “We’ll try out a few things. Perhaps Phonzy will be fine, just with restricted minutes. There’s a lot of rotation, a lot of movement, and the full-backs are involved in the attack. We’ve got plenty of players available there, which gives us options, as does our strong midfield. We’ll play as normal, in our usual style, finding solutions with different players. Who those players are, we’ll discuss that amongst the coaching staff. We’ll try a few things out and then see how it goes.”

item.title: Coach who helped Sinner to the top set to depart
item.description: Sinner (left), with Cahill, has not played since winning Wimbledon in July [Getty Images] The coach who helped guide Jannik Sinner to five Grand Slam titles and the world number one spot is to leave the player's camp at the end of the year. Australian Darren Cahill, 61, joined the Italian's team in June 2022 when Sinner was just outside the world's top 10 and had never progressed beyond the quarter-finals of a Grand Slam tournament. But, together with Italian coach Simone Vagnozzi, Cahill has helped Sinner to go on to win five Slams and occupy the world number one spot for 95 weeks. Injury has meant the 25-year-old has not played since winning Wimbledon for the second year in a row in July, which led to Alexander Zverev recently overtaking him at the top of the rankings. He is set to return to action at the Six Kings Slam tournament in Saudi Arabia next month. Swede Magnus Norman, the long-time coach of recently retired Stan Wawrinka, will join Sinner's team for next season. "Darren has been an incredibly important part of my journey," Sinner said. "Together with Simone and the whole team, we have achieved things I dreamed of growing up. "He has helped me grow both as a player and as a person, and his guidance will stay with me throughout my career." Cahill had originally planned to leave at the end of 2025, but told Sinner at Wimbledon that the Italian could decide whether he stayed on - as long as he won the title. "Working with Jannik has been a special honour and privilege," Cahill said. item.title: How to watch U.S. Open Squash Championships, new Olympic sport
item.description: The U.S. Open Squash Championships, a major international competition for a new Olympic sport, air Friday and Saturday on Peacock . The U.S. Open semifinals are Friday at 6 p.m. ET and the finals Saturday at 6 ET from Philadelphia. Squash was part of a group of sports added in October 2023 to the 2028 Los Angeles Olympic program, along with baseball, softball, cricket, flag football and lacrosse sixes. Squash is a racket sport where two players compete in an enclosed court with four walls. Matches are best-of-five games. The first player to 11 points, with at least a two-point lead, wins each game. The Olympic debut of squash in 2028 will feature men's singles and women's singles events with 16-player fields. The tournaments will be held at the Comcast Squash Center inside Universal Studios. At the U.S. Open, both sets of semifinals feature the world's top three ranked players: Mostafa Asal (Egypt), Paul Coll (New Zealand) and Diego Elias (Peru) for the men and Amina Orfi (Egypt), Hania El Hammamy (Egypt) and Nour El Sherbini (Egypt) for the women. The top Americans — world No. 5 Olivia Weaver and No. 10 Amanda Sobhy — lost in the round of 16. item.title: Ex-PSG star Diallo to stand trial for alleged assault on team-mate
item.description: Aminata Diallo (L) is accused of involvement in the attack on her ex-Paris Saint-Germain teammate Kheira Hamraoui (JAVIER SORIANO) Former Paris Saint-Germain women's star Aminata Diallo is to stand trial on charges relating to the assault on her ex-teammate in 2021, according to a court order issued Friday and seen by AFP. Diallo, 31, is believed by the investigating magistrate to have ordered the attack on her fellow former French international teammate and guided the attackers to where the assault took place. She is charged with complicity in violence and criminal conspiracy. Six others will go on trial alongside her. The date for the trial has yet to be announced. In November 2021, Hamraoui was attacked by two masked men, who hit her on her knees with iron bars, after returning from a team dinner in a car with Diallo. "After five long years of the case being investigated, it is a huge relief they have reached a conclusion and soon there will be a trial," Hamraoui's lawyers Julia Minkowski and Said Harir told AFP in a statement. "The whole truth will finally come out in this violent affair which is so rare in football, indeed sport, in which the victim was subjected to an unconscionable campaign of harassment following the assault." Diallo's defence team claimed there had been a lack of fairness in the investigation. "There has neither been a punishment nor questions posed about the methods used in the investigation regarding Aminata Diallo, which is also peppered with false statements," said Romain Ruiz, one of her four-lawyer defence team. "It's as if she has been crying in the desert for four years. We will call out her innocence till the final day of her trial." Hamraoui, 36, lost when she took PSG to a labour court last year claiming damages of 3.5 million-euro ($4m) alleging she was forced out of the club following the assault. Hamraoui was seeking damages from her former club, alleging a lack of support. She claimed she was "ostracised" on the pitch, in the changing room and suffered harassment on social media. item.title: McIlroy fires 63 to move into Abu Dhabi contention
item.description: Rory McIlroy is chasing a sixth successive Race to Dubai crown [Getty Images] Rory McIlroy put the setback of the two-shot penalty he received on Thursday behind him as he posted 11 birdies in shooting a nine-under-par second-round 63 at the Abu Dhabi Championship on Friday. McIlroy had been handed the sanction for improving his lie during the opening round and as a result finished day one on two under par, eight shots behind the leader, Italian Francesco Laporta. The six-time major winner was penalised after pressing down on the grass behind his ball with his club before hitting a chip on the par-four 12th at Yas Links. The Northern Ireland player responded in style in round two however to move to 11 under and assume the clubhouse lead with several of the leading players on the leaderboard still to complete their second 18 holes. McIlroy began his round with a bogey at the first but bounced back by picking up shots at the second, fourth and seventh holes. The back-to-back Masters champion then stormed up the leaderboard with five consecutive birdies from holes nine to 13. A dropped shot at the 14th proved to be only a temporary blip as he recorded two further birdies on the 17th and 18th holes to cap a scintillating round. It isthe first time in his career that he has made 11 birdies in a single round of a DP World Tour event. The 37-year-old is chasing a fifth Race to Dubai title in a row and a record-equalling eighth in total, that would draw him level with Scotland's Colin Montgomerie. McIlroy went into the Abu Dhabi tournament in third position in the standings, behind leader Eugenio Chacarra and second-placed Patrick Reed. item.description: Photo by Al Bello/Getty Images The New York Knicks saw their fair share of celebrities between opening night and their NBA championship run, and two of the stars have lightly called out Taylor Swift. One thing that the New York Knicks winning the NBA championship did for the NBA is bring the celebrities out in full force. The Knicks have some of the most famous fans in the country. Names like Timothee Chalamet, Ben Stiller, and Mariska Hargitay were seen courtside throughout their entire run. Arguably one of the biggest musical stars in the world, Taylor Swift, also made a few appearances to root for the team during the run. She wasn’t at nearly every game like a lot of the other celebs, though, and it has led to her getting an unfortunate shoutout from Tyler Kolek and Deuce McBride. item.title: Wolves legend Coady retires from playing, aged 33
item.description: Conor Coady made 317 of his 503 club appearances in a Wolves shirt [Shutterstock] Wolverhampton Wanderers legend Conor Coady has retired from playing at the age of 33. The former Wolves skipper, who won 10 England caps, has been linked with a move into coaching, having been without a club since leaving Wrexham in September. After beginning as a promising midfielder in the Liverpool academy, he moved first on loan to Sheffield United in 2013, before signing for Huddersfield Town at the end of that season. But he enjoyed most of his success at Wolves after being converted into a central defender by then boss Nuno Espirito Santo. He also played for Everton, Leicester City, Wrexham and on loan at Charlton last season in his 503-game club career. Coady was signed by then Wolves boss Kenny Jackett in 2015 - and played a major part in the club's promotion back to the Premier League in 2018. He captained the Wolves team who twice finished seventh and also reached the quarter-finals of the Europa League. In all, he made 317 Wolves appearances, scoring seven of his career tally - for club and country - of 22 goals, before being allowed to leave on loan for Everton in 2022. He then joined Leicester for a reported £8.5m in July 2023 after Everton opted not to complete a £4.5m deal to turn his season-long loan into a permanent switch. Coady then moved on to an ill-fated short spell at Wrexham , which was ended prematurely before his final move to The Valley , to join Nathan Jones' Charlton. item.title: Marc Marquez jokes Alex would be a 'bad brother' if he risked title fight
item.description: Motorsport photo Marc Marquez heads into this weekend's Qatar Grand Prix with a 44-point advantage over Jorge Martin and a 67-point advantage over Marco Bezzecchi , and with three rounds remaining, he has his first opportunity to secure the MotoGP world title at Lusail. But his championship lead could have been smaller had he not won at Sepang last Sunday. Marquez overtook his younger brother, who had secured pole position, at the start of the race. Apart from a brief moment on the opening lap, Alex Marquez made no serious attempt to regain the position and eventually dropped to third behind Pedro Acosta . Speaking in Qatar on Thursday, Marc Marquez insisted his brother had simply made a sensible decision, particularly given the physical difficulties he had been dealing with. "Alex has done a great job in the second half of the season, in the last few races," Marquez said. "Especially considering his physical condition. "In Malaysia, he was looking after his own interests and knew how to manage the risk. That's what brothers are for. "If your brother is fighting for a world championship, you're not going to throw your bike at him and see what happens. Even less so because we both ride Ducatis. "If you do that, then you're a bad brother. You have to call him and apologise." Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex Marquez, Gresini Racing Alex finished third in Malaysia to claim his third podium of the season. Afterwards, the Gresini rider confirmed he would undergo surgery the following day to remove the large plate supporting his right collarbone and address ongoing shoulder problems stemming from his heavy crash at Barcelona. The operation has ruled him out of the Qatar GP, leaving Marc without the potential support of his brother as he attempts to secure the championship. But the factory Ducati rider dismissed the suggestion that he needed help from other riders. "When you have the speed, you don't need wingmen, team orders or anything," he said. Marquez arrived in Doha later than most of his rivals, taking the last available flight that would allow him to attend Thursday's official press conference. Despite his sizeable championship advantage, he remained cautious about his chances of wrapping up the title this weekend. "I know the numbers. item.title: Newcastle's Dedic stopped by police after being spotted with bow and arrows
item.description: Amar Dedic has featured in seven Premier League games since joining Newcastle in August [PA] Newcastle United defender Amar Dedic was stopped by police after being spotted carrying a bow and arrows at a Northumberland beauty spot. Bosnia-Herzegovina international Dedic, 24, was with a friend when he was stopped in a car after a concerned member of the public raised the alarm. Reports say six police cars were dispatched, including armed police, and that Dedic and his companion were stopped about seven miles away from where they were originally spotted. Police searched the car and seized the bow and arrows but were satisfied the two men were not a threat to the public. BBC Sport has been told Dedic had no ill intention and has fully co-operated with police. It is reported Newcastle goalkeeper Mark Gillespie, 34, and former defender Paul Dummett, 35, arrived at the scene while police were speaking to Dedic. It is understood the pair were in the area by chance and stopped to offer assistance. The incident happened on Wednesday, two days after Dedic - who joined from Benfica for a fee in the region of £30m in August - had played in Newcastle's 1-0 home defeat by Everton. Newcastle, who are 13th in the Premier League table on 11 points from nine games, have not commented. Northumbria Police has released a statement and said enquiries are ongoing. The force has not named Dedic. It said it received reports of two men carrying a bow and arrows while walking along a track by the reservoir on Military Road in the Harlow Hill area. "Officers attended and subsequently stopped a vehicle in the Darras Hall area and seized a bow and arrows," added the statement. "At this stage, it is understood they were for recreational use and there was no threat to the public." Newcastle are at Fulham on Saturday (15:00 GMT) before the November international break. Dedic, who has featured in 10 league and cup games since joining Newcastle, has been named in the Bosnia-Herzegovina squad for Nations League matches away to Sweden on 14 November and at home to Romania on 17 November. item.description: Thomas Tuchel says he has “enough” No 10s in his England squad without selecting Cole Palmer , who has paid the price for pulling out of the September camp last time out and missing “too many opportunities to impress”. The Chelsea star was a notable omission from Tuchel’s 25-man squad ahead of the Nations League games against Croatia and Spain and he was available for selection. Tuchel criticised Palmer for missing “too many camps with injuries” following his withdrawal from last month’s group and the manager has opted to stick with many of the same players who impressed him last time. Tuchel has named several No 10s in his group, Morgan Rogers , Morgan Gibbs-White , Eberechi Eze , Jude Bellingham , as well as first-time call-ups Josh King and Jobe Bellingham, who both offer versatility in his midfield. Palmer has not played for England since March and was missed the World Cup after struggling with injuries last season. He has played in all nine of Chelsea’s Premier League matches this season, but was also sent off in the defeat to Tottenham. Speaking at a press conference at Wembley, Tuchel explained: “It counts when you are in camp and I just said it last time, he misses too many opportunities to impress. It was a long camp. It was two-and-a-half weeks and the players and the boys who were in camp built something extraordinary throughout these weeks. “That's why the credit goes to them. The trust is for them. If you are in camp, this is your chance to impress. So it's not personal. We will never assume that Cole is not in the mindset to come and desperate to play for his country, but the competition is on and the players who were in camp did an amazing job and kept their place.” Tuchel added: “There are enough of No 10s, and we stick to the guys who were in camp because camp was excellent and we were happy with the last two-and-half weeks that we had together. ”The impact of all the players was immense throughout the whole camp and that's why we stick mainly with the group. item.description: Tuchel hails ‘extraordinary’ Kane as England captain prepares to set all-time appearance record Thomas Tuchel has said England will celebrate 'an extraordinary player' as Harry Kane prepares to break the Three Lions' all-time record for appearances. Kane will make his 126th appearance for England against Croatia in the UEFA Nations League next week, moving ahead of Peter Shilton to take the outright record, after equalling the goalkeeper's mark last camp. Kane is already England's record scorer with 91 goals, the seventh-highest total in men's international football history. The 33-year-old's record-breaking feats continue an incredible period for Kane, who became England's first Ballon d'Or winner in 25 years last month. Kane has also signed a new deal at Bayern Munich this week. Speaking at a press conference on Friday, Tuchel said this month's fixtures are a chance to celebrate Kane and his achievements, though highlighted the importance of results for England. "Just an incredible achievement that these two occasions come together one after the other and we are able to witness this. "He wins the Ballon d'Or, deservedly so, and then gets the all-time record for England with 126 appearances in his next Engalnd game. "It's an important match for us. It is a crucial match for us, to set up a final in Spain after. "So it is a deserved frame and a deserved occasion to celebrate an extraordinary player."

item.description: Arsenal 18yo receives another senior international call-up Arsenal youngster Ceadach O’Neill has received another senior call-up from Northern Ireland, following his recent Gunners first-team debut. If he’s good enough to do that, it’s no surprise he’s also getting international opportunities. He’s since worked his way up through the u19s and u21s to reach the senior team, and he seems to be highly-rated by the first-team coaches.
